name: VanillaDB
tagline: Readable Java relational engine from NTHU for teaching database internals and prototyping research.
description: VanillaDB is a family of small, deliberately readable database components from the DataLab at National Tsing Hua University in Taiwan. VanillaCore is a single-node, multi-threaded relational engine in Java that supports part of SQL-92 and can be used through JDBC, embedded, or via Java stored procedures; VanillaComm adds group communication for distributed systems and VanillaBench provides TPC-C-style benchmarks. It is used in NTHU's database courses and as a research testbed, including the T-Part (SIGMOD 2016) work and the ElaSQL deterministic distributed database. Core releases stopped at 0.7.0 (2022), with only light activity since.
statusNote: Teaching/research system; VanillaCore last released 0.7.0 (Sept 2022) with sporadic commits since. Still usable for coursework.

scale.notes: Single node; distributed variants (e.g. ElaSQL) are separate research systems.

strengths: Clean, documented Java code that students can read end to end
Modular layers (storage, buffer, recovery, concurrency, planner) that are easy to swap
Used as a real testbed in published research
Companion benchmark and communication modules for distributed experiments
weaknesses: Not tuned or hardened for production
Small community; activity has slowed since 2023
useCases: Prototyping new concurrency or recovery algorithms
